name: com.midmanstudio.inventorizz
description: Game-agnostic container/inventory runtime on top of the DixScript (.mdix) database. Item and container-type definitions are mdix-authored content (Samples~/core/{enums,builders}.mdix, example_items.mdix); container INSTANCES are created at runtime by a host (InventorizzRuntime.CreateContainer), never derived automatically from the catalog -- a player can own several backpacks of the same type, the way Questly's quests or HudMan's HUD items never could. Zero game-specific logic: item taxonomy is entirely free-form tags (ItemDefinition.Tags), never a closed enum, unlike the two genuinely structural/mechanical enums this package does declare (StackPolicy, CapacityKind) via plain @ENUMS -- neither is a per-game catalog a consuming game needs to extend, so the ScriptableObject-provider pattern HudMan/GenSettings use for their catalogs doesn't apply here. Every container is internally a positionally-addressable slot list; SLOT_COUNT/WEIGHT_AND_SLOTS types pre-allocate a fixed, never-resized array (real empty slots, stable indices -- what a grid-style drag-and-drop UI needs), UNLIMITED/WEIGHT types start empty and grow on add (no fixed cells, capacity is a pure aggregate check). TryAddItem is deliberately best-effort (fills as much as actually fits, reports how much via an out param) since a loot-and-carry game generally wants 'grab what you can carry' rather than an all-or-nothing failure; TryTransferItem is its atomic sibling (snapshot-and-rollback, all-or-nothing) for when a partial result would be the wrong call. Ships with a real dragndrop (com.midmanstudio.dragndrop) integration: plain-C# IDraggable/IDropTarget logic classes (zero UnityEngine dependency, directly testable against the real DragDropController) plus thin MonoBehaviour wrappers pairing with dragndrop's own UGUI adapter components -- an exact-slot target for grid UIs, a whole-container target for flat-bag UIs or as a fixed-grid catch-all. Same hybrid persistence model as Questly/HudMan: CaptureState/RestoreState (host-owned POCO) and SaveToMdix/LoadFromMdix (package-owned file), with a shrunk fixed-grid container's out-of-range saved slots dropped gracefully on restore rather than crashing. Does not subscribe to the catalog's DefinitionsChanged itself -- there's no well-defined 'reconcile all instances' operation the way Questly has for quests, since instances aren't derived from the definition set in the first place; a host hot-reloading content alongside live instances needs its own reconciliation policy. No enum-generator Editor tooling (StackPolicy/CapacityKind are plain closed enums, not provider-generated, so none is needed). Instances also support an optional lock: IsLocked/SetLocked/ContainerLockChanged. While locked, TryAddItem/TryRemoveItem/TryRemoveFromSlot/TryMoveStack all fail (mutate nothing) against that instance -- TryTransferItem inherits this for free through the two calls it already makes. Not persisted (a host recomputes what should be locked, e.g. from current location, rather than trusting a stale saved flag); CreateContainer/DestroyContainer are unaffected, since locking blocks player-initiated content changes, not administrative lifecycle.
